ORAL JUDGMENT 1.

The present appeal is filed by the appellants-original claimants challenging the judgment and award dated 24.09.2021 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, at Lunawada in M.A.C.P.
No.2826 of 2017.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2. The short facts leading to filing this First Appeal is that on NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4190/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 16/02/2023 undefined 13.07.2017, deceased Vikramsinh was coming from Santrampur to his Village in a Chhakado rickshaw, driven by its driver slowly,
carefully in moderate speed and on the correct side of the road.

At about 16.30 hours, near Bhilodiya Talav at Village:Nani Sarsan on Santrampur to Lunawada road, the opponent no.1 came by driving S.T.Bus No.GJ.18.Z.0988 in rash and negligent manner with an excessive speed, and therefore, lost control over steering, the S.T.Bus left the road and came on extreme wrong side and dashed with the chhakado in which the deceased was traveling.
As a result, the deceased sustained severe injuries and succumbed to the injuries.
3. It is stated that the deceased was doing Centing Work at the time of accident.

The deceased was the only earning member of the family of the 7 persons and thus, considering the "Consumer Price Index" and the "cost of inflation index" in the Year-2017, the monthly income ought to have been considered accordingly.
Therefore, it is urged that Rs.8000/- per month would be considered as monthly income of the deceased.
Further, the ground has been raised that no consortium money has been granted to the claimants.

4. Mr.Nishit Bhalodi, learned advocate for the appellants- original claimants relying the judgment of Apex Court in case of New India Assurance Co.Ltd. Vs. Smt.Somvati & Others [Civil Appeal No.3093 of 2020], Magma General Insurance Co.Ltd. Vs. Nanuram @ Churu Ram & Ors.

The future prospective rise has been granted as 25% to the income so assessed and the claimants have been awarded Rs.40,000/- towards the loss of consortium and in total an amount of Rs.9,36,250/- has been computed as total compensation.

In the case of Magma General Insurance Company Limited Vs. Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram & Ors., reported in (2018) 18 SCC 130, it has been observed as under:-
"8.7

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Company Limited Vs. Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram & Ors., reported in (2018) 18 SCC 130
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: A Constitution Bench of this Court in Pranay Sethi (supra) dealt with the various heads under which compensation is to be awarded in a death case.
One of these heads is Loss of Consortium.
In legal parlance, "consortium" is a compendious term which encompasses 'spousal consortium', 'parental consortium', and 'filial consortium'.

The right to consortium would include the company, care, help, comfort, guidance,
solace and affection of the deceased, which is a loss to his family.
With respect to a spouse, it would include sexual relations with the deceased spouse.
(Rajesh and Ors. vs. Rajbir Singh and Ors. (2013) 9 SCC 54)

entities.label: PRECEDENT

BLACK'S LAW DICTIONARY (5th ed. 1979)

Parental consortium is granted to the child upon the premature death of a parent, for loss of "parental aid, protection, affection,
society, discipline, guidance and training."
Filial consortium is the right of the parents to compensation in the case of an accidental death of a child.
An accident leading to the death of a child causes great shock and agony to the parents and family of the deceased.
The greatest agony for a parent is to lose their child during their lifetime.
Children are valued for their love, affection, companionship and their role in the family unit.
Consortium is a special prism reflecting changing norms about the status and worth of actual relationships.
Modern jurisdictions world-over have recognized that the value of a child's consortium far exceeds the economic value of the compensation awarded in the case of the death of a child.
Most jurisdictions therefore permit parents to be awarded compensation under loss of consortium on the death of a child.
The amount awarded to the parents is a compensation for loss of the love, affection, care and companionship of the deceased child.
The Motor Vehicles Act is a beneficial legislation aimed at providing relief to the victims or their families, in cases of genuine claims.
In case where a parent has lost their minor child, or unmarried son or daughter, the parents are entitled to be awarded loss of consortium under the head of Filial Consortium.

Parental Consortium is awarded to children who lose their parents in motor vehicle accidents under the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4190/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 16/02/2023 undefined Act."
8.
Here in this case, the appellants are four, who are the children of the deceased hence, considering the consortium amount per head as 40,000/- i.e. Rs.1,60,000 (40,000 X 4) is granted.
9. In view of the judgment of the Pranay Shetti (supra), the amount under funeral expenses and loss to estate is considered as Rs.15000/- each.
10. The claimants thus, would be entitled to an amount, as under the following head:-

Future Loss of Income Rs.12,12,792/-
 Loss of consortium Rs.1,60,000/-
 Loss of estate Rs.15,000/-
Funeral expenses Rs.15,000/-

The Tribunal has granted Rs.9,36,250/- lacs as compensation money at the rate of 9% interest, the appellants would be entitled to enhanced amount of compensation of Rs.4,66,542/- at the rate of 7.5% interest per-annum, which the G.S.R.T.C. is directed to deposit within eight weeks from the date of receipt of writ of this Court.
The award be modified accordingly.
